ios.alerts_errors_collapse.note: Screen-reader name of a row of the Alerts tab that groups the device's errors, while its list of errors is shown: tapping it hides the list. {title} is the first error's title, written by the device (already in the user's language); {count} is how many errors the row holds. Lowercase collapse, as the end of the phrase.

ios.alerts_errors_expand.note: Screen-reader name of a row of the Alerts tab that groups the device's errors, while its list of errors is hidden: tapping it shows the list. {title} is the first error's title, written by the device (already in the user's language); {count} is how many errors the row holds. Lowercase expand, as the end of the phrase.

ios.alerts_friends.note: Beside a check mark, at the right of a friend request in the Alerts tab once you accepted it from there: you are friends now.

ios.bluetooth_needed_hint.text: Allow Bluetooth for Off The Cloud in Settings to set a device up this way.
ios.bluetooth_needed_hint.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): under the heading Bluetooth access is needed. Settings is the iPhone's own Settings app: use its name in this language.

ios.bluetooth_off_hint.text: Turn Bluetooth on in Control Centre to find the device.
ios.bluetooth_off_hint.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): under the heading Bluetooth is off. Control Centre is the iPhone's: use iOS's own name for it in this language.

ios.compose_capture_save_failed.text: Couldn't save the capture to Photos: {detail}
ios.compose_capture_save_failed.note: Alert in the New Post composer when a photo or video just taken with the camera couldn't be saved to the iPhone's Photos library. {detail} is the system's reason (in the iPhone's language).

ios.compose_capture_unreadable.text: The capture was saved to Photos but couldn't be read back.
ios.compose_capture_unreadable.note: Alert in the New Post composer when a photo or video just taken with the camera was saved to the iPhone's Photos library but couldn't be added to the post.

ios.compose_photo_unreadable.note: Why a post couldn't be published, after app.social.compose.publish_failed_detail: a photo picked from the iPhone couldn't be read to upload it.

ios.compose_source.note: Screen-reader name of the Phone / Synced switch at the top of the New Post composer: where the photos shown come from.

ios.compose_upload_failed.note: Why a post couldn't be published, after app.social.compose.publish_failed_detail: a photo picked from the iPhone couldn't be uploaded to the device, which gave no reason.

ios.compose_video_unavailable.text: This video is not available on the phone
ios.compose_video_unavailable.note: Why a video picked from the iPhone couldn't be opened for trimming in the New Post composer (shown after app.social.compose.trim_load_failed): Photos couldn't hand it over (for example it is only in iCloud and couldn't be downloaded).

ios.connection_superseded.text: The connection settings changed; try again.
ios.connection_superseded.note: Error given to an action whose connection attempt was overtaken by new connection settings (saved, or a Log Out) while it was on its way.

ios.download_bad_piece.text: The device sent a piece that doesn't fit the file
ios.download_bad_piece.note: Why opening or downloading a file failed (after Download failed: or similar): a piece the device sent doesn't match the file's size or place.

ios.download_changed.text: The file changed on the device during the download
ios.download_changed.note: Why opening or downloading a file failed (after Download failed: or similar): the file was replaced on the device while it was being fetched.

ios.file_type_label.note: Screen-reader name of a document icon in the Files grid. {type} is what the icon shows: a type such as PDF, DOC or ZIP, or a file extension in capitals.

ios.files.allow_deletions.note: Confirm button of the question app.files.allow_deletions_title (Files, a tap on an upload-only folder's lock): lets the folder's files be deleted again. Title Case in English.

ios.files.gallery_copied.note: What the Copy Link button (app.files.gallery_copy_link) of the Share as Gallery sheet says once the link was copied.

ios.files.gallery_counting.note: Shown with a spinner when the Share as Gallery sheet opens, while the device counts what will be shared.

ios.files.gallery_expires.note: Heading of the choices of how long the gallery's link works (1, 7 or 30 days) in the Share as Gallery sheet, and the screen-reader name of those choices.

ios.files.gallery_job_failed.text: The gallery could not be created
ios.files.gallery_job_failed.note: Error in the Share as Gallery sheet when the device stopped copying with an error and gave no reason (when it gives one, its own words are shown instead).

ios.files.gallery_keep_open.text: Keep this screen open: the link is shown here once the copy is done.
ios.files.gallery_keep_open.note: Under the progress bar of the Share as Gallery sheet while the device copies the photos and videos.

ios.files.gallery_link_once.text: This link is shown only now - the device never stores it. Send or copy it before closing.
ios.files.gallery_link_once.note: Under the gallery's link in the Share as Gallery sheet once the gallery is ready.

ios.files.gallery_nothing.text: There are no photos or videos to share here.
ios.files.gallery_nothing.note: Under the disabled Share button of the Share as Gallery sheet when the folder or collection has no photos or videos.

ios.files.gallery_skipped.note: Second line of the Share as Gallery sheet, before sharing, when the folder holds files that aren't photos or videos: they won't be in the gallery. {count} is how many. In English both forms are the same.

ios.files.gallery_starting.note: Shown with a spinner in the Share as Gallery sheet right after Share is tapped, until the device starts copying.

ios.files.keep_out_of_images.note: Confirm button of the question app.files.keep_out_title (Files: Keep out of Images in the bar, with one folder selected): keeps the folder's photos and videos out of Images (not tagged, not searched for faces; the tags and faces already found are deleted). Title Case in English. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

ios.files.make_upload_only.note: Confirm button of the question app.files.make_upload_only_title (Files, a tap on a folder's open lock): makes the folder upload only. Title Case in English. Upload only: nothing in the folder can be deleted, and uploading a file again keeps its older version.

ios.files.older_versions.note: Screen-reader name of the badge with a clock and a number on a file in Files: how many older versions the device keeps of it. A tap lists them.

ios.files.result_file.note: Screen-reader name of a file (not a photo or video) in the results of a search in Files and in the search suggestions (Images, or the top bar on a wide screen). {name} is its file name, {folder} the folder it is in (a path such as /Photos/2024).

ios.files.result_file_kept_out.text: {name}, file in {folder}, kept out of Images
ios.files.result_file_kept_out.note: Screen-reader name of a file (not a photo or video) in the results of a search in Files when its folder is kept out of Images. {name} is its file name, {folder} the folder it is in. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

ios.files.result_folder.note: Screen-reader name of a folder in the results of a search in Files and in the search suggestions (Images, or the top bar on a wide screen). {name} is its name, {folder} the folder it is in (a path such as /Photos/2024).

ios.files.result_folder_kept_out.text: {name}, folder in {folder}, kept out of Images
ios.files.result_folder_kept_out.note: Screen-reader name of a folder in the results of a search in Files when it is kept out of Images (its photos and videos aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown there). {name} is its name, {folder} the folder it is in. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

ios.files.result_photo.note: Screen-reader name of a photo in the results of a search in Files and in the search suggestions (Images, or the top bar on a wide screen). {name} is its file name, {folder} the folder it is in (a path such as /Photos/2024).

ios.files.result_photo_kept_out.text: {name}, photo in {folder}, kept out of Images
ios.files.result_photo_kept_out.note: Screen-reader name of a photo in the results of a search in Files when its folder is kept out of Images. {name} is its file name, {folder} the folder it is in. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

ios.files.result_video.note: Screen-reader name of a video in the results of a search in Files and in the search suggestions (Images, or the top bar on a wide screen). {name} is its file name, {folder} the folder it is in (a path such as /Photos/2024).

ios.files.result_video_kept_out.text: {name}, video in {folder}, kept out of Images
ios.files.result_video_kept_out.note: Screen-reader name of a video in the results of a search in Files when its folder is kept out of Images. {name} is its file name, {folder} the folder it is in. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

ios.files.try_again.note: Button under the error shown in place of the results of a search in Files: searches again. Title Case in English.

ios.friends_delete_theirs.text: Delete everything from {name} on this iPhone
ios.friends_delete_theirs.note: Switch (off at first) when removing a friend: also deletes everything of theirs from your device (explained by app.social.friends.delete_theirs_text). {name} is the friend's profile name (or their device's address when they have none).

ios.friends_remove_friend.note: Button (in red) at the foot of the Remove (a friend)? screen: removes the friend, deleting what its two switches say.

ios.menu_close.note: Screen-reader name of the dimmed page behind the left menu laid over it (on a wide screen): tapping it closes the menu.

ios.no_answer_slow.text: The device isn't answering. It may be off, or the connection may be too slow.
ios.no_answer_slow.note: Why the app can't connect, on the card shown over the app: the connection to the device stopped answering while signing in.

ios.open_settings.note: Button in Set up a new device (over Bluetooth) under ios.bluetooth_needed_hint: opens the iPhone's Settings at this app's page, where Bluetooth can be allowed. Settings is the iPhone's own app: use its name in this language.

ios.photos_access_denied.note: Alert in the full-screen photo viewer when Save was tapped but the app isn't allowed to add photos to the iPhone's Photos library.

ios.photos_download_failed.note: Alert in Images when the link to download the selected photos as a zip (the selection bar's Download) couldn't be made. {detail} is the reason (the app's or the system's own words).

ios.photos_people_deleting.note: At the foot of the People page while several people are being deleted: which one is being deleted ({current}) of how many ({total}).

ios.photos_people_face_to_keep.note: Screen-reader name of the group of faces to choose from in the merge's box (People page).

ios.photos_people_merge_hint.note: Screen-reader hint on the dimmed Merge item of the bar shown while one face is picked on the People page.

ios.photos_people_new_name.note: Screen-reader name of the field that renames a person who already has a name, under their face on the People page.

ios.photos_search_documents.note: Screen-reader name of the row of the search suggestions that lists, in Files, every file and folder whose path contains what was typed (app.photos.search.documents). {text} is the typed text.

ios.photos_search_key_hint.note: Screen-reader hint on the highlighted row of the search suggestions: the keyboard's Search key takes that row.

ios.photos_search_person_in.note: Screen-reader name of a person in the search suggestions who is already a chip in the search. {name} is their name, {count} how many photos show them. Otherwise it is app.photos.people.face_label.

ios.photos_search_suggestions.note: Screen-reader name of the list of suggestions under the search field (Images, or the top bar on a wide screen).

ios.photos_upload_failed.note: Alert in Images when a photo that is only on this iPhone couldn't be uploaded to the device before sharing it, downloading it or adding it to a collection. {detail} is the reason (the app's or the system's own words).

ios.plist.cfbundlename.note: The app's bundle name (Info.plist CFBundleName). Never translated.

ios.plist.nsbluetoothalwaysusagedescript.text: Used to set up a new Off The Cloud device next to you, before it has joined your WiFi.
ios.plist.nsbluetoothalwaysusagedescript.note: iOS permission prompt (Bluetooth), shown by the system when the app first uses Bluetooth: why the app needs it.

ios.plist.nscamerausagedescription.text: Used to take a photo or video to post to your feed
ios.plist.nscamerausagedescription.note: iOS permission prompt (camera), shown by the system when the app first uses the camera: why the app needs it. No full stop in English.

ios.plist.nslocalnetworkusagedescription.text: Off The Cloud connects to your own device on your home network to sync photos and files.
ios.plist.nslocalnetworkusagedescription.note: iOS permission prompt (local network), shown by the system when the app first reaches the device on the home network: why the app needs it.

ios.plist.nsmicrophoneusagedescription.text: Used to record sound with videos you post to your feed
ios.plist.nsmicrophoneusagedescription.note: iOS permission prompt (microphone), shown by the system when the app first records a video: why the app needs it. No full stop in English.

ios.plist.nsphotolibraryaddusagedescript.text: Used to save photos from the gallery viewer, and photos and videos you take to post, to your Photos library
ios.plist.nsphotolibraryaddusagedescript.note: iOS permission prompt (adding to Photos), shown by the system the first time the app saves a photo to the library: why the app needs it. Photos is Apple's Photos app. No full stop in English.

ios.plist.nsphotolibraryusagedescription.text: This app needs access to your Photos to back them up
ios.plist.nsphotolibraryusagedescription.note: iOS permission prompt (Photos library), shown by the system the first time the app reads the photo library: why the app needs it (it backs the photos up to the user's device). No full stop in English.

ios.settings.albums.note: Row in Settings > Sync Options that opens the list of the iPhone's albums in the Photos app (the user's own, and Screenshots, Selfies...) with a switch for each, and that screen's title. These are Apple's albums, not Off The Cloud's collections: use the Photos app's own word.

ios.settings.albums_all.note: Value at the right of the Albums row in Settings > Sync Options when no album is turned off: every album is backed up. Agrees with albums.

ios.settings.albums_empty.text: There's nothing to choose from yet: every photo on this iPhone is backed up.
ios.settings.albums_empty.note: On the Albums screen (Settings > Sync Options > Albums) when the iPhone has no album holding photos.

ios.settings.albums_footer.text: Everything is backed up except the photos in albums you turn off, even when those photos are in other albums too. Turning an album off only stops backing it up: nothing is deleted, from this iPhone or from your device. Turning it back on backs up everything already in it.
ios.settings.albums_footer.note: Under the list on the Albums screen (Settings > Sync Options > Albums): a photo in an album turned off isn't backed up, even if an album that is on holds it too; and what turning a switch off, and on again, does. These are the Photos app's albums, not Off The Cloud's collections. Your device is the Off The Cloud device.

ios.settings.albums_off.note: Value at the right of the Albums row in Settings > Sync Options: how many albums are turned off, so not backed up. Agrees with albums.

ios.settings.bridge_leave_delete.note: Button (in red) of the confirmation Delete your account?: the device leaves the bridge, then the account page opens to delete the account.

ios.settings.crop_hint.text: Drag the photo to centre your face.
ios.settings.crop_hint.note: Under the circle on the screen Crop photo.

ios.settings.crop_title.note: Title of the screen that crops the new profile photo to a circle.

ios.settings.free_up_footer.text: Photos and videos older than that are deleted from this phone, each only once the device confirms it holds an exact copy. Edited photos and bursts stay: the device has only their original. iOS asks before deleting, and they stay in Recently Deleted for 30 days. With iCloud Photos on, they also go from iCloud and your other devices. This happens after a sync while the app is open, at most once a day.
ios.settings.free_up_footer.note: Under the Free Up Space section on iPhone (Settings, and the Sync Your Photos sheet): what its switch does. "older than that": older than the time chosen just above (Older than 7 days). Recently Deleted and iCloud Photos are Apple's names: use the ones iOS shows in your language.

ios.settings.free_up_live_photos.note: Switch in the Free Up Space section on iPhone: Live Photos are deleted from the phone too. Live Photo is Apple's name: use the one iOS shows in your language.

ios.settings.free_up_live_photos_detail.text: The device keeps only the still picture of a Live Photo, so its motion is lost once it's deleted here.
ios.settings.free_up_live_photos_detail.note: Under the Include Live Photos switch: why it is off unless turned on. The sync sends only a Live Photo's still picture to the device, not its few seconds of motion.

ios.settings.links_delete_message.text: Delete this link? The shared copies are deleted and the link stops working.
ios.settings.links_delete_message.note: Message of the confirmation asked before deleting a shared link (its title is app.settings.links.delete_title).

ios.settings.logs_picker.note: Screen-reader name of the choice at the top of the Logs screen between the Device and Updates logs.

ios.settings.logs_read_failed.note: Error on the Logs screen when the log couldn't be read and the device gave no reason; the app tries again.

ios.settings.logs_send_failed.note: Error in the form that sends the logs when they couldn't be sent and the device gave no reason.

ios.settings.logs_troubleshooting.note: Heading of the section of Settings holding the Logs row.

ios.settings.picker_empty.note: Shown on the screen Choose a photo when the chosen collection (or the device) has no photo.

ios.settings.picker_error.note: Error on the screen Choose a photo when the tapped photo couldn't be fetched. {detail} is why, as the system or the connection words it.

ios.settings.picker_load_failed.text: Couldn't load that photo from your device.
ios.settings.picker_load_failed.note: Error on the screen Choose a photo when the tapped photo couldn't be fetched and the device gave no reason.

ios.settings.picker_open_failed.note: Error on the screen Choose a photo when the tapped photo arrived but couldn't be read as a picture.

ios.settings.profile_from_iphone.note: Item of the Change photo menu in Settings > Profile: pick the profile photo in the iPhone's Photos.

ios.settings.profile_unexpected.note: Shown for a few seconds in Settings > Profile when the device answered the save with something the app didn't expect.

ios.settings.sync_icloud.note: Switch in Settings > Sync Options: also upload photos whose original is only in iCloud (the iPhone downloads them first).

ios.settings.thumbs_title.note: Heading of the section of Settings about the small pictures of the photos kept on this iPhone so Images opens fast.

ios.setup_language_later.text: The setup page will switch to {language} once the installation starts.
ios.setup_language_later.note: iPhone app, setting up a device over Bluetooth: a line over the setup page (the web page the device serves) after the language was changed with the screen's language menu while that page was already open. The page of a device with older software changes language only once the device starts installing, so that nothing typed on it is lost; until then it stays in the language it opened in. {language} is the newly chosen language, written by its own name (for example Español, Deutsch); language names are never translated.

ios.setup_signin_cancelled.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): error given to the setup page when the person closed the Apple or Google sign-in.

ios.storage_details_hidden.note: Screen-reader value of the Storage row at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen) while the storage details under it are hidden.

ios.storage_details_shown.note: Screen-reader value of the Storage row at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen) while the storage details under it are shown.

ios.storage_gauge_attention.note: Screen-reader name of the storage ring in the icon rail (on a wide screen) while the device's fullness isn't known and a disk stopped working or the device reports a problem.

ios.storage_gauge_hint.note: Screen-reader hint of the storage ring in the icon rail (on a wide screen): pressing it opens the whole menu at the storage details.

ios.storage_gauge_used.note: Screen-reader name of the storage ring in the icon rail (on a wide screen). {percent} is how full the storage is, already formatted (45%).

ios.storage_gauge_used_attention.note: Screen-reader name of the storage ring in the icon rail (on a wide screen) when a disk stopped working or the device reports a problem. {percent} is how full the storage is, already formatted (45%).

ios.storage_needs_attention.note: Screen-reader name of the red dot by Storage at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen): one disk of the mirror stopped working or the device reports a problem.

ios.storage_percent.note: Screen-reader value of the storage bar at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen): how full the storage is. {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100.

ios.storage_used.note: Screen-reader name of the bar at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen) that shows how full the device's storage is.

ios.trim_cant_title.note: Heading in the Trim video screen of the New Post composer when the video can't be opened; why follows under it (app.social.trim.cant_open or app.social.trim.no_length).

ios.trim_end_handle.note: Screen-reader name of the right handle of the two-handle slider in the Trim video screen: where the part of the video kept for the post ends. Its value is read as a time (0:12.5).

ios.trim_play_cut.note: Button (with a play symbol) in the Trim video screen of the New Post composer: plays only the part of the video that will be kept.

ios.trim_start_handle.note: Screen-reader name of the left handle of the two-handle slider in the Trim video screen: where the part of the video kept for the post starts. Its value is read as a time (0:02.0).

ios.wallpaper_album_name.note: Name of the album the app makes in the iPhone's Photos app for a collection used on the lock screen. {name} is the collection's name. Keep Off The Cloud as it is.

ios.wallpaper_album_ready.note: Once the album in the Photos app holds the copies. {count} is how many photos it has. Followed by the steps (ios.wallpaper_steps_title).

ios.wallpaper_full_access.text: To make the album, Off The Cloud needs access to all your photos. You can allow it in Settings.
ios.wallpaper_full_access.note: When the app has limited or no access to the iPhone's photos: making the album needs full access, given in the iPhone's Settings app (use its name in your language: Ajustes, Réglages, Einstellungen, Impostazioni, Definições, Instellingen). A button that opens Settings follows.

ios.wallpaper_lock_button.note: Button under ios.wallpaper_lock_text: stores the copies in the Photos app album. Says they are stored, on purpose.

ios.wallpaper_lock_text.text: The copies go into an album in the Photos app, “{album}”, and also show in your library there. If iCloud Photos is on, Apple uploads them to iCloud too. Photo Shuffle on the lock screen then rotates them.
ios.wallpaper_lock_text.note: Under ios.wallpaper_lock_title, before anything is stored: the copies go into the iPhone's Photos app (and its library), and to iCloud if iCloud Photos is on; the lock screen's Photo Shuffle then shows them. {album} is the album's name (ios.wallpaper_album_name). Use iOS's own names for Photos, iCloud Photos and Photo Shuffle in your language; if unsure, describe them. Use this language's quotation marks.

ios.wallpaper_lock_title.note: Heading of the lock screen part of the iPhone wallpaper screen (ios.wallpaper_title). Use iOS's word for the lock screen.

ios.wallpaper_step1.text: Touch and hold the lock screen, then tap +.
ios.wallpaper_step1.note: First step to set the album as the lock screen. Use iOS's own words for touch and hold.

ios.wallpaper_step2.text: Tap Photo Shuffle, then Album, and choose “{album}”.
ios.wallpaper_step2.note: Second step: Photo Shuffle is the lock screen's own option that rotates photos (iOS 17.1 and later can use an album). Use iOS's own name for it in your language; if unsure, describe it. {album} is the album's name (ios.wallpaper_album_name).

ios.wallpaper_step3.text: Pick how often the photo changes, and confirm.
ios.wallpaper_step3.note: Third step: Photo Shuffle offers on tap, on lock, hourly or daily.

ios.wallpaper_steps_title.text: Now set it on your lock screen
ios.wallpaper_steps_title.note: Heading over the three steps that set the album as the lock screen (ios.wallpaper_step1-3): apps can't do it themselves.

ios.wallpaper_stop_album.note: Button while the collection has its album in the Photos app: deletes the album and the copies in it.

ios.wallpaper_stop_album_note.text: The album and its copies are deleted from the Photos app; iOS asks you to confirm.
ios.wallpaper_stop_album_note.note: Under ios.wallpaper_stop_album: iOS itself asks before photos are deleted from the Photos app.

ios.wallpaper_stop_widget.text: Stop the widget and delete its copies
ios.wallpaper_stop_widget.note: Button while the collection's copies for the widget are stored: deletes them (the widget then asks for a collection again).

ios.wallpaper_title.note: Title of the screen opened by Use as wallpaper… (app.photos.wallpaper.menu) on iPhone: two ways to show the collection's photos, on the lock screen (through an album in the Photos app) and in a home screen widget. {name} is the collection's name. Use this language's quotation marks.

ios.wallpaper_widget_button.note: Button under ios.wallpaper_widget_text: stores the copies for the widget. Says they are stored, on purpose.

ios.wallpaper_widget_ready.text: Ready. Add the widget to your home screen.
ios.wallpaper_widget_ready.note: Once the widget's copies are stored. Followed by ios.wallpaper_widget_steps.

ios.wallpaper_widget_steps.text: Touch and hold the home screen, tap Edit, then Add Widget, choose Off The Cloud, and pick this collection.
ios.wallpaper_widget_steps.note: Shown once the widget's copies are stored: how to add the widget. Use iOS's own labels (Edit, Add Widget) in your language.

ios.wallpaper_widget_text.text: The copies stay in Off The Cloud's own space on this iPhone, never in the Photos app. The widget shows a different one every hour.
ios.wallpaper_widget_text.note: Under ios.wallpaper_widget_title, before anything is stored: the widget's copies are kept by the app itself (not in the Photos app, not in iCloud); the photo changes every hour.

ios.wallpaper_widget_title.note: Heading of the widget part of the iPhone wallpaper screen (ios.wallpaper_title). Use iOS's word for the home screen.

ios.widget_choose.text: Touch and hold to choose a collection.
ios.widget_choose.note: Inside the widget while no collection is chosen yet (touch and hold the widget, then Edit Widget).

ios.widget_description.text: A photo from one of your collections, a different one every hour.
ios.widget_description.note: Description of the widget in the iPhone's widget gallery.

ios.widget_name.note: Name of the app's home screen widget in the iPhone's widget gallery, and the title of its setting that picks the collection. Our word for a named group of photos.

ios.widget_not_stored.text: Open this collection in Off The Cloud and choose “Use as wallpaper…” to store its photos here.
ios.widget_not_stored.note: Inside the widget when its collection has no copies stored for it yet (or they were deleted). The quoted part is app.photos.wallpaper.menu, written the same way. Use this language's quotation marks.

ios.ws_connect_timeout.text: The device didn't answer the connection in time.
ios.ws_connect_timeout.note: Error given to an action when the connection to the device couldn't be opened in time (nothing answered at its address).

ios.ws_still_connecting.note: Error given to an action whose time ran out while the app was still connecting to the device.

ios.ws_timed_out.text: The device didn't answer in time.
ios.ws_timed_out.note: Error given to an action (and shown on the card shown over the app when connecting fails) when the device didn't answer a request in time.

ios.ws_unresponsive.text: The connection to the device stopped answering.
ios.ws_unresponsive.note: Error given to the actions waiting on the connection to the device when it stopped answering and was closed; the app connects again.
